heading: SAE feature analyses can fail to preserve model behavior when error terms are omitted
definition: analyses built on SAE features (circuits, steering) lose a meaningful share of the model's behaviour unless the error term is kept.
summary: Independent studies find that some SAE feature circuits depend on retained error terms, but the general claim is contested. Other settings preserve behavior without them, with dependence varying across layers, architectures and tasks.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for unqualified V5 at <1B and 1–10B; setting-specific error dependence has independent supporting evidence at both scales. ? at 10–100B and >100B. Synthetic formal-language results include support and counterexamples, but counts do not identify a separate toy-size bucket.
suggested_status.reason: Independent circuit evidence supports error dependence in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B (arXiv:2403.19647#r20, arXiv:2403.19647#r21). Counterexamples include early–middle GPT-2 attention layers (lw:EGvtgB7ctifzxZg6v#r1, #r10), preserved Expr validity (arXiv:2410.11767#r14, #r20), and near-preserved SmolVLA success (arXiv:2603.19233#r07). These contest the universal wording while leaving conditional support intact. counts: versions.V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V5.studies_by_size covers <1B, 1-10B and not stated; versions.V5.verdicts.challenges.studies = 5.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched circuit and steering comparisons should establish which tasks, layers and SAE recipes require error retention, using explicit behavioral thresholds and the same edits with error retained or dropped. Comparable tests above 10B would change the scale assessment. Matched π0.5 checkpoints and hook configurations would clarify the cross-study discrepancy.

source.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Joshua Engels; L. Smith; Max Tegmark

original_result.setup: On Gemma 2 9B layer 20, the study replaced activations with SAE reconstructions plus linear or nonlinear error components, using either 16k-wide SAEs or SAEs with about 60 active features (L0).
original_result.result: Linear and nonlinear error components each contributed to downstream cross-entropy increases roughly in proportion to their size. The linear component may have contributed slightly more.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Gemma crosscoder dictionaries left substantial behavioral differences unexplained without the chat model’s reconstruction error.
Removing attention SAE errors disrupted behavior at several layers.
Residual SAE errors carried substantial subject–verb agreement circuit function in Gemma-2 2B.
Replacing Gemma-2-2B residual activations without SAE errors increased loss and impaired MMLU performance.
Removing all SAE errors severely reduced subject–verb agreement circuit faithfulness.
GPT-2 Small attention reconstructions disrupted indirect object identification at early and late layers.
SAE reconstruction substantially reduced language validity across many tested architectures and training choices.
Gemma Scope reconstruction reduced Gemma 2 2B MMLU accuracy across every tested domain.
SAE reconstruction reduced robot policy success, with severe losses for some pooling methods.
Dropping SAE errors added enough noise to mask changes caused by perturbing clinical features.
OpenVLA success collapsed without SAE errors despite high explained variance.
Early response tokens relied more on crosscoder dictionaries than on error terms.
SAE errors explained a minority of attention-score variance in the tested decomposition.
SAE error ablation mattered less in late layers and attention or MLP components.
Improved SAE training reduced reconstruction damage and recovered fluent generation.
Attention and MLP error removal was less disruptive when residual errors remained.
GPT-2 Small attention SAEs preserved indirect object identification across layers 1–6 without errors.
A top-k SAE retained high English validity without its error term.
ESM2-3B's added cross-entropy loss approached zero as SAE sparsity decreased.
SAE reconstruction barely changed ViT-Small head-pruning accuracy or head usage.
Some robot policies lost little success under SAE reconstruction.
EEG encoder reconstructions generally preserved classification AUROC, with small losses in early LaBraM layers.
OpenVLA success roughly halved without the SAE error near the action head.
Reconstructed steering toward weddings weakened at medium intervention strengths but improved slightly at other strengths.
Early-middle attention SAE reconstructions preserved behavior with little contribution from errors.
Top-k SAE reconstructions preserved Expr validity without error terms.
ESMFold SAE reconstruction caused little structural accuracy loss on filtered CASP14 targets.
SmolVLA and mean-pooled GR00T reconstructions largely preserved rollout success.
π0.5 retained baseline success across probed layers without SAE errors.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Error-dependent circuit, steering or reconstruction behavior in models in the 10–100B and >100B size buckets.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size contains <1B, 1-10B and not stated, with no 10-100B or >100B entry. The pack supplies no explicitly sized tests in those larger buckets.

untested.what: How error dependence changes across training stages in a matched model lineage with the task, SAE recipe and intervention held fixed.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_stage and versions.V5.coverage_by_operation list stage coverage but no matched training trajectory. The base/chat crosscoder experiment measures a behavioral difference between models; it does not compare stage-specific dependence under an otherwise fixed SAE analysis.

wording_issues.phrase: analyses built on SAE features (circuits, steering)
wording_issues.issue: Direct circuit evidence exists, but much supporting evidence measures whole-layer replacement loss, grammatical validity, output KL or rollout success. Those results do not directly measure the behavior omitted by a circuit explanation or a steering analysis.

The records provide no common threshold or denominator. Small IOI error-ablation effects, preserved Expr validity and statistically indistinguishable EEG AUROC coexist with large circuit-faithfulness and rollout losses.

wording_issues.phrase: unless the error term is kept
wording_issues.issue: Error retention is not universally necessary for the tested behavior: early–middle GPT-2 attention layers, Expr top-k reconstruction and π0.5 reconstruction hooks preserve their respective task metrics without it.

The endpoints capture different aspects of behavior. Preserved structure accuracy can coexist with divergence between protein predictions; EEG AUROC measures a coarse ranking task, while crosscoder KL measures output-distribution differences. These cannot be treated as interchangeable behavioral shares.

method_sensitivity.what: In Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B subject–verb agreement circuits, removing all SAE error nodes is more disruptive than removing only attention/MLP error nodes while retaining residual errors; this comparison does not isolate residual-error-only removal. Faithfulness magnitudes are figure-only. In Gemma-2-2B SVA-RC, layers 14–17 have the largest four-layer ablation effect, but early–middle four-layer ablations retain faithfulness above 0.7. Late windows beginning at layer 18 have little effect under the no-restoration condition. The layer-24 finding uses feature restoration and should not be equated with those sliding windows.

GPT-2 Small IOI reconstruction preserves approximately clean logit difference at layers 1–6, produces notable drops at layers 0, 7 and 8, and can increase logit difference at later layers despite high KL. Endpoint choice therefore affects whether reconstruction appears faithful. The preserved reconstruction conditions challenge meaningful behavioral loss in those settings. Separately, zero-ablating the layer-5 error term at S2 on ABBA prompts changes logit difference by −0.048, versus −0.826 for the top feature: a small nonzero effect, without an established negligible or nonsignificant effect.

method_sensitivity.factor: SAE training objective, encoder and normalization
method_sensitivity.what: For Gemma-2-2B base with all residual layers replaced, encoder tuning included and validation on 1 million tokens, Gemma Scope gives KL 1.66864 and CE 2.714; replacement-aware LISTA with full-replacement fine-tuning gives KL 0.378151 and CE 0.758738. Base CE is 0.387681: training changes degradation magnitude, while meaningful behavioral loss remains. In formal-language Expr models, L1 architecture-I reconstruction retains 33.31% grammatical validity, while top-k architectures I and III retain 99.88% and 99.76%, respectively, against clean validity above 99%. Architecture I has no normalization; architecture III uses input normalization. Table entries average over hidden sizes and sparsity settings. The preserved top-k Expr settings challenge meaningful loss on this metric; they do not establish preservation across languages or architectures.

The text-based verdict reports large ESM2-3B layer-18 ΔCE at very low L0 and near-zero ΔCE above L0 100. Reconstruction-induced functional loss cannot be specified independently of sparsity. No extracted row records the sweep.

For Gemma-2-2B base/chat crosscoders at layer 13, using either L1 or BatchTopK, All replacement—chat reconstruction plus base error—recovers 59% of the output-KL gap over full responses and 78% over tokens 2–10. Error replacement uses base reconstruction plus chat error. Error produces slightly lower output KL than All over full responses, but more than twice All's KL divergence over tokens 2–10. This ranking change does not negate meaningful error dependence: the verdict reports approximately 22% of baseline KL remains unrecovered by All on early tokens.

method_sensitivity.factor: VLA architecture, pooling, write-back and depth
method_sensitivity.what: The VLA comparison reports near-preserved SmolVLA success but larger losses in OFT, and much worse mean-pool replacement in some architectures. Its text reports that residual write-back retaining the error avoids mean-pool collapse on OFT, GR00T and X-VLA. In OpenVLA, late reconstruction hooks are less disruptive than earlier hooks, but layer-31 reconstruction-only success remains 34.8 ± 24.5% versus 68.0 ± 14.3% raw success. This substantial behavioral loss supports V5; depth changes its magnitude.

For fine-tuned EEG encoders evaluated on binary normal/abnormal AUROC, LaBraM's maximum layer-wise drop is 0.017, and performance improves with substitution depth. Early-layer statistical significance is not explicitly reported. Across all LaBraM layers, mean ΔAUROC is 0.006 ± 0.006, a partial effect; statistical indistinguishability is stated only from layer 4 onward. Every tested SleepFM and REVE layer is also described as statistically indistinguishable from baseline. Those explicitly indistinguishable settings challenge meaningful functional loss on this endpoint.

The GPT-2 XL wedding-vector comparison favors the original vector at medium norms but slightly favors reconstruction-only steering at large or small norms. The finding is qualitative and has no extracted row.
